status: draft -03 text; held for ratification with -03
inputs: controller_bindings and binding_revocations are delivered beside the containing Bundle. Each History card is illustrative: no verifier of these vectors reads its counts.

cases.description: Two parties' halves of one exchange joined on the exchange identifier, and each party's History answer joined to its own party's half on same_key. Each History's envelope verifies under its responder, its artifact and request digests match, its card states the anchor its envelope names, and its anchor checkpoint is that checkpoint and verifies. Each History's key is the key under which its party's root record's producer signature verifies: agree. Every observer is in its own custody domain, yet each same_key agreement is redundant: one key answered and signed for both members. The halves corroborate on declared custody. Each History's time is after its party's root record, reported as a fact.

The reference composition with history-b anchored before responder-b's root record: the History responder-b could show when it agreed. The tie is the key alone, so the join still derives agree; the verifier reports history-b's time as before the record's, as a fact with no join state.

history-a joined to responder-b's half on same_key and declared agree. history-a's key is responder-a's; responder-b's root record verifies under responder-b's key. The keys differ: the verifier derives unjoined and reports both keys. The declaration does not match the derivation: a failed check.
The same join declared unjoined: the verifier derives unjoined and reports both keys.

responder-b's root record states responder-a's key in key_id, but its producer signature was made by responder-b's key. A same_key join reads a key only from a signature that verifies under it, never from what the record states, so responder-b has no key: the join with history-a is not_derivable, never agree.
responder-a's root record carries no producer signature: it gives no key, and the same_key join with history-a is not_derivable.

The reference composition with history-a declared missing: its body is withheld, its id, observer, request digest, outcome and digest stay in the composed digest, which equals history-two-parties. Composition closure is withheld, and the join naming history-a is not_derivable.
history-a carries a checkpoint other than the one its envelope's anchor.digest names. The member fails; it has no join view, so its join is not_derivable.
history-a's envelope signature was made by another key than its responder: the member fails, and its join is not_derivable.
history-a's card states another anchor than its envelope's anchor.digest: the member fails, and its join is not_derivable.

history-a's envelope names a profile whose member names and signature this revision does not read: signature-unverified, neither failed nor absent. It has no join view, so its join is not_derivable and the block is withheld.
history-a's envelope signs an artifact_digest that is not the SHA-256 of its artifact octets: the member fails, and its join is not_derivable.
history-a's envelope answers another request than the member's request_digest names: the member fails, and its join is not_derivable.
history-a's anchor checkpoint is the one its envelope names, but its signature does not verify: the member fails, and its join is not_derivable.

history-a's anchor checkpoint carries an entry in its unprotected header. Its signature still verifies, but it is not the one form the interop profile fixes for a checkpoint (tagged COSE_Sign1, an empty unprotected header): the member fails, and its join is not_derivable.
history-a's artifact is the card with whitespace, not its JCS serialization: it does not state its anchor in the one form a History artifact takes, so check 4 fails.
history-a's envelope profile is an array, not a profile identifier: the verifier reads no profile it implements, so the signature is unverified and the block is withheld.

history-a's envelope passes all five checks, but its digest is not the member digest the block declares. It is not the History the composed digest names: composition closure fails and it has no join view.
history-b joined on same_key to responder-a's empty-history Bundle, whose checkpoint responder-a's key signed. The keys differ: unjoined, as declared, and the verifier reports both keys.
history-a is listed in missing but still carries its body: composition closure fails. A join naming it still derives from the carried body.

responder-a refused its half (a signed refusal, signature-unverified with no deployment profile). history-a's same_key join with that refusal: one member is an artifact with records, the other is not an artifact, so the join is one_sided, as declared. The refusal's signature is unverified, so the block is withheld.

responder-a answered with an empty-history Bundle whose stream's first checkpoint responder-a's key signed. Under same_key its key is that checkpoint's signer, the same key as history-a's responder: linked, and only one member has records, so one_sided, as declared. No root record, so no History times.
A pre_agreed_identifier join between history-a and responder-a. A History has no root record, and this revision defines no derivation for a History member on that basis: not_derivable, not malformed.

history-a and history-b joined by controller_binding: one binding record over the two responder keys, both keys signed it, in effect at both anchor times. Each History's key and T are its join view; T only tests the binding's window. No pointer is needed between two Histories. Linked: agree, redundant (controller_binding).

A controller_binding join of history-a and responder-b carrying compare. The binding applies to history-a's responder key at its anchor time and the key responder-b's root record names at its timestamp: linked. The compare pointer resolves in responder-b's root record and never in a History, so the join derives mismatch, as declared.
history-a's envelope names a record subject, not full_history: the history body is malformed, and so is the block.
history-a carries a response beside its history body. The envelope is the History's response and is digest-covered; a response member beside it is not: malformed.
history-a carries both a history and a bundle body: an artifact member carries at most one. Malformed.
history-a's anchor_checkpoint is unpadded base64url whose pad bits are not zero: it decodes to the same octets as the canonical text, so it is not the one form -03 allows. Malformed.
A same_key join carrying pointer. same_key reads each member's own key and carries none of pointer, identifier_digest and compare: malformed.
